money_at_stake.rationale: The occurrence is a circuit split over which regulatory regime governs sports-related event contracts, i.e. whether this revenue is captured through state-licensed sportsbooks or through CFTC-lane prediction-market exchanges. The pool in contention is the U.S. sports-wagering revenue pool itself: AGA-sourced 2025 data (found via a reachable industry-press source after both originally cited sources stayed unreachable this run; see basis) puts U.S. sports betting revenue at just shy of USD 17 billion for the year, on a total wagering handle of USD 166.9 billion, sitting inside a total U.S. commercial gaming revenue base of USD 78.7 billion. Either figure, taken as the annual revenue pool this ruling's outcome helps direct, lands inside the USD 10-100 billion band, well clear of the USD 1 billion floor and nowhere near the USD 100 billion ceiling, so B10_100 is not a close call on the boundary.
money_at_stake.basis: Both sources originally cited for this leg stayed unreachable this run: the AGA 'State of the States 2026' report page (americangaming.org/resources/state-of-the-states-2026/) returned HTTP 403 on two direct-fetch attempts and the direct PDF (americangaming.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/AGA-State-of-the-States-2026.pdf) exceeded this tool's fetchable size limit; the CoinDesk article carrying Kalshi's disclosed revenue run-rate returned HTTP 429 on four attempts across three URL variants; Wayback Machine is categorically unreachable from this tool for both domains. Rather than repair either citation with a substitute for the SAME claim (forbidden), I searched for and fetched a different, independently reachable source stating the same underlying AGA figures: CDC Gaming's 2026-03-13 article, which quotes the AGA release directly and was fetched and quoted fresh this run (see evidence). This is a secondary industry-press source restating AGA's primary report, tagged INFERRED rather than VERIFIED for that reason; the AGA report and PDF themselves remain unopened. I did not pursue a Kalshi-specific figure further because the AGA sports-wagering total alone already places this leg inside B10_100 with room on both sides, so a second figure would not move the band. Re-run candidates if a tighter figure is wanted later: retry americangaming.org directly (403 on this kind of page is often a transient WAF block), retry the CoinDesk URL after its rate limit clears, or look for Kalshi's own investor/blog disclosure of its revenue run-rate rather than routing through a news aggregator.

public_reach.rationale: Mixed and clearly reachable, held at 65 rather than higher because the fastest-growing entity in the story is unlisted. The regulated-sportsbook side is priced by the market in real time: DraftKings and Flutter Entertainment both rose the same session the Ninth Circuit ruled against Kalshi's sports event contracts (DraftKings +6.5%, Flutter +4.6%), which is a listed issuer's exposure to this exact occurrence being priced live. On the prediction-market side, Robinhood is the one clean listed proxy: its event-contracts (transaction) revenue reached USD 156 million in Q2 2026 and, for the first time, exceeded its own crypto-trading revenue (USD 100 million that quarter), so real money in this exact vertical is already landing on a brokerage-reachable ticker. Not scored higher because the dominant operator on the prediction-market side, Kalshi, is privately held (per the occurrence record) rather than listed, and I could not this run re-verify Kalshi's specific funding-round size, valuation, or market-share claim after the only citation for those figures (a CoinDesk article) returned HTTP 429 on repeated attempts; those specific numbers are dropped from this file rather than asserted without a source I actually opened.

evidence.claim: Robinhood's event-contracts (transaction) revenue rose to USD 156 million in the second quarter, up more than USD 50 million from the prior quarter and up from practically nothing a year earlier, marking the first quarter in which event-contract revenue exceeded Robinhood's crypto transaction revenue, which came in at USD 100 million that quarter, down USD 60 million year over year.

source_excerpt: Robinhood saw its transaction revenue from event-based contracts soar to $156 million in the second quarter, up over $50 million from the prior quarter and from practically nothing just one year ago.
This is also the first quarter in which event-based contracts revenue exceeded crypto transaction revenue, which came in at $100 million in the second quarter, down $60 million from one year ago.

capture_odds.rationale: Genuinely open, so scored near the middle rather than rounded toward either side's story. For capture: the market itself priced this as a profit event immediately, with a same-day stock move in the listed sportsbook names (see public_reach), and the occurrence's own framing is a fee pool that keeps converting into disclosed revenue on some venue regardless of which regulatory regime ultimately wins. Against capture: the underlying legal question is one circuit's ruling, not an industry-wide settlement, so whichever side is capturing today could see that reversed at a higher court. The industry's own economics also cap how much of gross activity becomes durable profit: state gaming taxes took a record USD 18.09bn out of 2025's USD 78.72bn total commercial gaming revenue (up 15.1% and 9.2% respectively), and heavy promotional spend has historically compressed sportsbook margins below headline revenue growth. Not scored lower, because real money is already sticking as disclosed revenue on the regulated-sportsbook side today, cited above. Note: the prior version of this leg's rationale cited a specific Third-Circuit-conflict / Supreme-Court framing to a CNBC article that returned HTTP 403 this run with no Wayback fallback; that specific citation is deleted, and the general circuit-split framing is carried here only as the occurrence's own established anchor fact, not as a newly sourced claim.

evidence.claim: U.S. commercial gaming revenue reached a record USD 78.72 billion in 2025, a 9.2 percent increase, while state-regulated gaming generated a record USD 18.09 billion in gaming tax revenue, up 15.1 percent year over year.
evidence.source_name: PR Newswire (American Gaming Association), Commercial Gaming Revenue Hits $78.7 Billion in 2025, Driving Record $18.1 Billion in Gaming Taxes Nationwide
source_excerpt: The U.S. commercial gaming industry reached a record high in 2025, generating $78.72 billion in gross gaming revenue (GGR), a 9.2 percent increase over the previous year.

In 2025, legal, state-regulated gaming generated $18.09 billion in gaming tax revenue, supporting state and local education, infrastructure, and other services across the country, up 15.1 percent over last year.

timing_fit.rationale: Money is already moving, not merely projected: the listed sportsbook names repriced the same trading day the ruling issued (DraftKings +6.5%, Flutter +4.6%), so part of this occurrence's effect landed on day zero. Raised back from 75 to 80 this run because the SCOTUS-timeline reasoning, uncited since the 2026-08-30 excerpt-repair pass deleted its only source, now has a dated citation: New Jersey filed its petition for a writ of certiorari on 2026-09-02, one day ahead of the 2026-09-03 deadline, expressly naming the new Ninth Circuit ruling as creating a 'direct, acknowledged, and irreconcilable split between the Third and Ninth Circuits.' That is the forcing event actually landing inside the appraisal window, not merely a deadline that might have lapsed: the case is now docketed for the Supreme Court to act on (grant, deny, or hold), and a cert-to-decision cycle for a case of this profile typically runs on the order of one to two years, which lands comfortably inside the 2 to 5 year window this repo underwrites. Interim quarterly disclosures from Robinhood and the listed sportsbook operators will keep marking progress well before then. Not scored higher because certiorari itself is not yet granted, so the multi-year regulatory-resolution clock is confirmed as moving rather than confirmed as bounded.
